observations:
LM2 Torah 33 is too short and conceptually sparse to support the formation of independent packages from the source text alone. The Torah covers 8 lines and makes one essential conceptual move: distinguishing between bodily joy and soul-joy, with the soul's תכלית (ultimate end) being unambiguously good while the body — depending on its origin — may or may not share in that joy.

For a new package proposal, the spec requires 3+ concepts connected by EXPLICIT bechina language forming an independent domain. LM2 Torah 33 contains no explicit bechina language whatsoever — the word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear in the text.

The closest thing to a bechina structure in this Torah is the identification of three terms: 'סוֹף כָּל סוֹף' (the ultimate end) = 'הַתַּכְלִית' (the purpose) = 'טוֹב מְאֹד' (very good). But this is a single three-way equation of synonyms, not a network of distinct concepts connected by bechina relationships across independent domains.

The Torah's two potential conceptual axes — (A) שמחה / תכלית / נשמה (the good/soul axis) and (B) גוף / גר / טיפה טמאה (the body/purity axis) — are connected to each other by EITZA relationships (the origin of the body CAUSES the inability to rejoice bodily), not by bechina. These two axes are eitza-related pairs, not bechina clusters that would form packages.

Conclusion: No new packages can be responsibly proposed from this Torah without first entering bechina edges into the dataset. If and when the dataset is enriched with LM2 Torah 33 data, the following two packages would likely emerge:
- Package A (good): שִׂמְחָה / תַּכְלִית הַטּוֹב / נְשָׁמָה — the soul-domain of ultimate joy
- Package B (neutral/good-evil split): גּוּף / גֵּר / טִפָּה טְמֵאָה — the body-domain split between holy body (tzaddik) and impure-origin body (ger)
